requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
The code carries out every obligation, but one named case has no test. That case is the "when available" condition on the status and error code in the final error.

**Obligations and code**
- **Stop retrying when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive transient failure.**
  - `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff]/fn[retry]` records the time of the first consecutive failure and a count of attempts in `failing`.
  - It stops when `now + delay > first + RETRY_LIMIT`. `RETRY_LIMIT` is 60 seconds.
  - The delay comes from `next_delay`. It takes the larger of the jittered window and any provider `Retry-After`, so a `Retry-After` that would pass the minute also stops retrying.
  - Non-transient errors return `Retry::Stop` with their own error.
- **Fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts.** The stop error says "after {attempts} attempts". `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` returns that error from the `Retry::Stop` arm.
- **Name the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.** `retry` builds the text from `failure_codes`. It has four forms:
  - "HTTP {status} {code}" when both are present.
  - "HTTP {status}" when only the status is present.
  - The code alone when only the code is present.
  - `error.to_string()` when neither is present, as with a timeout.
- **Reset after success.** `converse` creates a fresh `ProviderBackoff` after each successful response, so the first-failure time and count do not carry over.

**Tests**
`retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute` covers three things:
- A repeated 429 `ThrottlingException` stops within the minute. The error names the attempt count and "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException".
- A `Retry-After` of 90 seconds stops at once.
- A permanent error stops without the "kept failing" message.

**Gap**
- The text says the error names the status and code "when available". This is a case the text names, and the code has a separate branch for each combination.
- The test only exercises the branch where both the status and the code are present.
- No test asserts the stop error when only the status, only the code, or neither is available. A timeout failure is the case with neither.
- I searched `src` for "kept failing", "minute after" and `failure_codes` and found no other test covering these branches. Nothing excuses the omission, so these obligations are untested.

There is no `{fixme}` acknowledging the gap.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
